scenario: AITA for feeling annoyed that my boyfriend's mom kept some of my clothes meant for donation? | I believe I'm technically not in the wrong because this is all in my thoughts and I haven't vocalized this or made it evident, but I wanted to see if I'm justified in the way I feel. I kept a running donation box for 6 months in my apartment, and would periodically throw clothes in there when I felt ready to donate them. There were a lot of clothes in there near the end and they ranged from more inexpensive stuff like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive clothes from Ann Taylor and J.Crew. Nothing extremely expensive/designer, but there were clothes in there that were barely worn or still with tags on them. I thought it'd be nice to donate everything; not to mention, I didn't have time to even think about selling them. My BF and I have been together for 5 years, and his little sister (20yo) is a similar size as me, maybe one size larger (XS vs. S). It did cross my mind that I could've given some clothes to her, but 1) I've already done that in the past with two nice coats, 2) she's never displayed a ton of appreciation for gifts, 3) their family is not hurting for $, with an income of \~$1m. His mom came over, noticed the box, and asked what it was about, so I explained that I'd been wanting to donate the clothes. She said, "Oh! I could just drop it off at the donation center in \[underserved town next to hers\], if you'd like?" I thought that was really generous of her, and took her up on the offer after double checking it was not a chore for her. Anyway, I saw his parents again weeks later and mom said, "You had some pretty decent stuff in there! I took and saved some for \[sister\]." I can't help but feel totally annoyed with this. On one hand - yes, mom was kind enough to drop it off for me. On the other hand - the clothes were meant to be donated. So.. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out if I'm AITA (Am I The Asshole) in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, the scenario: I've been keeping a donation box for six months, collecting clothes to donate. These clothes range from cheaper brands like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive ones like Ann Taylor and J.Crew. Some of them are barely worn or still have tags on. I didn't have time to sell them, so donating seemed like a good idea. My boyfriend's mom noticed the box and offered to drop it off at a donation center in an underserved town. I appreciated her offer and agreed, making sure it wasn't a hassle for her. Weeks later, she mentioned that she took and saved some clothes for her daughter, who is a similar size to me. Now, I'm feeling annoyed because the clothes were meant to be donated, not kept by her family. So, why am I feeling this way? Well, the clothes were in a donation box, which implies they were meant to be given away to those in need. When his mom took some for her daughter, it felt like she took advantage of the situation. I had already given her the option to donate, and she chose instead to keep some for her family. That makes me feel like she didn't respect my intention to donate them. I also considered giving clothes to her sister before but decided against it for a few reasons: I had already given her two nice coats, she doesn't seem very appreciative, and their family is financially stable with a high income. So, I felt it was better to donate to those who might need them more. Now, is it wrong of me to feel annoyed? On one hand, his mom was helpful by offering to donate the clothes. On the other hand, she took some for her daughter, which goes against my original intention. I think it's reasonable to feel upset because she didn't follow through with donating all the clothes as I intended. It's like she used the opportunity to take something for her family without asking me first. I also wonder if I should have been more explicit about my intentions. Maybe if I had told her that all the clothes were meant to be donated and that I didn't want any kept, she wouldn't have taken them. But I didn't say anything, so perhaps I'm partly responsible for the misunderstanding. However, I did explain that the clothes were meant for donation when she asked about the box. She offered to drop them off, which I accepted. So, I think it's fair to expect that she would follow through with donating all of them. Taking some for her daughter without asking feels like she overstepped. In conclusion, I think it's justified to feel annoyed because my intention was to donate the clothes, and she took some for her family without my consent. It's okay to feel upset about that because it goes against what I wanted to happen with my belongings.
